title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is headed 'Cristaux'. It opens the divided-power (PD) foundations that Grothendieck's crystalline programme needs, treating the simplest case: a principal ideal J = πA.

Formally, one would want (πy)^n/n! = (π^n/n!) y^n. Grothendieck therefore asks for elements π^(0)=1 and π^(n) ∈ πA (n ≥ 1) satisfying three relations, marked (*):
(i) π^(1) = π.
(ii) π^(m) π^(n) = ((m+n)!/(m! n!)) π^(m+n).
(iii) π^(p) (π^(q)/π)^p = ((pq)!/(p!(q!)^p)) π^(pq).

A struck-out first attempt worries about an ambiguity: if πz = 0, then x = πy = π(y+z). This is resolved because every π^(n) (n ≥ 1) lies in πA, so π^(n) z = 0. The same argument covers (iii): π^(q)/π is defined only up to π-torsion, but after multiplying by π^(p) ∈ πA the product is well defined.

Grothendieck then defines γ_n(πy) = π^(n) y^n and asserts that this is a PD structure on J, independent of the choice of y. Checking the PD axioms:
- γ_n(ax) = a^n γ_n(x) is immediate.
- γ_m γ_n = binomial · γ_{m+n} follows from (ii).
- γ_n(x+x') = Σ γ_i(x) γ_{n-i}(x'): expand π^(n)(y+y')^n and compare with π^(i) π^(n-i) using (ii).
- γ_p(γ_q(x)) = ((pq)!/(p!(q!)^p)) γ_{pq}(x): write γ_q(πy) = π · (π^(q)/π) y^q and use (iii).
So the construction is correct.

Example 1: A is Z-torsion-free. Then π^(n) = π^n/n! is forced; Grothendieck says its existence is equivalent to π^n ∈ n!A for n ≥ 2, and that (*) holds automatically (check in A⊗Q).

Example 2: A_0 = Z_(p) and π = p. Here p^n/n! lies in pZ_(p), with valuation at least 1. Hence every Z_(p)-algebra A (residue characteristics only p and 0) gets a canonical PD structure on pA by specialisation, with p^(n) = p^n/n!. The page breaks off mid-sentence.

This is the standard basic example underlying crystalline cohomology over W(k) and Z_(p): it is what makes (Z_p, pZ_p) a PD base.
errors: Example 1 is incomplete as stated. 'Existence equivalent to π^n ∈ n!A for all n ≥ 2' ignores the requirement, imposed earlier on the page, that π^(n) ∈ πA (i.e. γ_n(J) ⊂ J). Counterexample: in the divided-power polynomial ring A = Γ_Z(π) ⊂ Q[π], one has π^n ∈ n!A for all n, but π^2/2 = π·(π/2) is not in πA, since π/2 ∉ A. The correct condition, for π not a zero divisor, is π^(n-1) ∈ n!A, i.e. π^n ∈ n!·πA.
Minor: the condition γ_n(J) ⊂ J and the full set of PD axioms are not verified on the page, only asserted ('on trouve'); they do follow from (*).

ideas.what: Criterion for a PD structure on a principal ideal πA via elements π^(n) ∈ πA satisfying multiplicativity and composition relations; well-definedness despite π-torsion
ideas.modern_name: Divided power structure on a principal ideal
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in the divided-power theory of Cartan, Roby (1963-65) and Berthelot (thesis, LNM 407, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the PD preliminaries of 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES 1966 notes by Coates–Jussila, in Dix exposés, 1968); Berthelot LNM 407 ch. I treats PD structures in general

ideas.what: Torsion-free case: π^(n) = π^n/n! is forced and the relations hold automatically
ideas.modern_name: PD structures in Z-flat rings are unique if they exist
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Berthelot; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology)

ideas.what: Canonical PD structure on pA for any Z_(p)-algebra A, with p^(n) = p^n/n!
ideas.modern_name: Canonical PD structure on (Z_(p), pZ_(p)) and on W(k)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), divided-power preliminaries

deep.surprise_reason: These are foundational, routine PD-structure computations, now standard in Berthelot's theory. The only point of note is a small slip in Example 1, where the condition π^(n) ∈ πA is omitted from the claimed equivalence. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Fouillons pour y définir' should read 'Formellement, pour y définir des puissances divisées, on est amené à définir des ...'.

Example 1 text is duplicated in the transcription; it reads: 'Alors les relations π^n = n! π^(n) définissent uniquement les π^(n) en fonction de π, et leur existence équivaut au fait que π^n ∈ n!A ∀ n ≥ 2.'
'alors une algèbre sur A_0' should read 'i.e. une algèbre sur A_0' (or 'donc une algèbre sur A_0').
'on n'a que x=πy' is likely 'tel que x = πy' / 'en vertu de x = πy'; the sense is that x^(n) does not depend on the choice of y with x = πy.
The three-line system of relations is labelled (*) by a marginal mark, which Example 1 later refers to.
